ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square, and the centers of the four circles are respectively located at the four vertices of the square. The two large circles are located at the two endpoints of one diagonal of the square, and the two small circles are located at the two endpoints of the other diagonal. In the figure the two large circles are tangent to each other, and a large circle is tangent to the small circle at an adjacent vertex. Reasoning: Let the side length of the square be s, the radius of a large circle be R, and the radius of a small circle be r. The centers of the two large circles are on a diagonal of the square, so their center distance is s√2. Because the two large circles are tangent, s√2 = 2R, therefore s = √2R. The center distance between an adjacent large circle and small circle equals the square side length s; they are tangent, so s = R + r. Substituting s = √2R gives R + r = √2R, therefore r = (√2 - 1)R. So the required factor is R/r = 1/(√2 - 1) = 1 + √2.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: a square is drawn with four circle centers at its four vertices; the large circles are centered at opposite vertices of the square, and the small circles are centered at the other two opposite vertices. Let the square side length be s, the big radius be R, and the little radius be r. From the image/text, the two big circles touch each other, so the distance between their opposite-corner centers is the square diagonal, s√2, and equals 2R. Hence s = √2 R. Also, each big circle touches a neighboring little circle whose centers are adjacent square corners, so their center distance is the square side s and equals R + r. Thus R + r = √2 R, giving r = (√2 - 1)R and therefore R/r = 1/(√2 - 1) = 1 + √2.
